title: This Fish Snaps Up Prey in 2 Milliseconds, Faster Than Any Blink

scenes.text: This fish snaps up prey in two milliseconds.
That's one of the fastest feeding strikes ever recorded in fish.
It's a snipefish, with a long tube for a snout.
It bends its head down, then snaps it back like a slingshot.
Scientists measured the strike at two to seven and a half milliseconds.
A human blink takes about a hundred milliseconds. You lose.

description:
This fish snaps up prey in two milliseconds.
Snipefish store energy in an elastic slingshot in their head, then release it to capture prey in two to seven and a half milliseconds.
What other animal do you think is faster? Comment below.
first_comment: Seahorses feed with the same kind of snap. Which animal would you pick as the fastest hunter?
